visual_subject: The two implementation routes the source names — manual watering beside automatic irrigation
rationale: 'Kaedah Pelaksanaan' has no subject beyond the methods it groups. The composite IS the two method visuals shown together, so it consumes no additional asset. The heading still receives a visual — the composite.

visual_subject: A rubber hose with a spray nozzle in use
rationale: Hose and spray nozzle — the equipment the source names.

visual_subject: Sprinkler system beside drip irrigation — broad turf coverage against emitters at individual root zones
rationale: Sprinkler against drip in one frame. The two systems are LIST_ITEM rows, not headings, so they were never separate obligations; they are the two halves of this one.

visual_subject: PENDING — this heading groups four unrelated management topics and has no subject of its own in the source
rationale: A grouping heading with no body text of its own. Its four management topics each carry their own obligation and their own visual; a separate visual for the header would have to invent a subject the source does not supply. Class is PENDING_HUMAN precisely because no subject can be derived.

visual_subject: A watering schedule showing early-morning and late-afternoon slots, with midday excluded
rationale: Watering schedule with early-morning and late-afternoon slots.

visual_subject: Water supply and pressure across a site — source, delivery and the pump and timer the contractor maintains
rationale: Site-wide water supply, pressure, pump and timer.

visual_subject: The signs the source names — wilted dry leaves for under-watering against yellowed leaves and root rot for over-watering
rationale: Under-watering against over-watering; both failure directions must be in one frame or the teaching point is lost.

visual_subject: Water cost against watering method on a large project
rationale: Water cost against watering method.

visual_subject: Granular fertiliser spread evenly around the root zone or across turf

visual_subject: Small holes dug around a tree's root zone, fertiliser placed in and covered back
rationale: Dig, place, cover — a three-step action needing sequence in one frame.

visual_subject: Liquid fertiliser sprayed directly onto foliage
rationale: Liquid fertiliser onto foliage — distinguishes leaf from soil application.

rationale: Specification check and S.O. approval shown as a gate.

visual_subject: Fertiliser stored dry, secured and away from any water source

visual_subject: A fertilising record showing date, fertiliser type, quantity and area treated

visual_subject: The IPM priority order — cultural, physical and biological control ahead of chemical

visual_subject: Good maintenance practice as prevention — correct watering and balanced fertilising

visual_subject: Patios, decks and plazas in use, with gazebos, benches and landscape lighting
